findings.title: RL-A-STAIR fascia posts stand 2.9in inside ST-S2A's 36in flight: R311.7.1 FAILs are real, not a check bug

evidence.measured: RL-A-STAIR posts (3x3, z 240..282) occupy y 69.64..72.64 at x 351-354, 302.9-305.9, 254.9-257.9; flight edge is y 69.75, so 2.89in intrudes. Tread tops under them are ~166/~200/234in, so post z lies 40-80in above the tread (inside the R311.7.1 36in zone). Clear between posts = 36 - 2.89 = 33.11in; past handrail = 36 - 2.89 - 3.45 (RL-A-HANDRAIL projection) = 29.66in. The check's own arithmetic reproduces both.
evidence.expected: >= 36in clear above handrail height and >= 31.5in past the one handrail
evidence.method: pickled resolved model; solids with host_ref RL-A-STAIR/RL-A-FLIGHT-GUARD, outline min/max in inches; stair_width.py _flight_projections logic by hand. scratchpad geometry-review/S1/p5.py

findings.source: IRC R311.7.1 (MN 2020 residential); attic.py comment says posts 'stand 3.036in into the well ... (code.R311_7_1, TODO)'; houses/catlin/CLAUDE.md records the FAILs as open
findings.proposed_fix: Posts must not stand in the flight: RL-A-STAIR is fascia-mounted on the well face (offset 0), so its posts hang into the well over the flight. Either top-mount the posts on the 3.5in trimmer pack/study side of y=69.625 (S3 owns the product/mount), or set the post line south so its inboard face is on y<=69.75. RL-A-FLIGHT-GUARD already stands outboard (y 66.73..69.73) and is fine. The check logic is correct (only posts reaching tread+34..+80 count).
